content: This medication may increase the risk of developing blood clots, particularly if you are using an estrogen-containing product. It can also cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin and face, a condition known as melasma. Exposure to sunlight can exacerbate this effect, so it is recommended to limit sun exposure and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while using this medication. Some estrogen products contain mineral oil, which can weaken rubber-based products such as latex condoms, cervical caps, and diaphragms, potentially leading to their failure. If you are unsure whether your product contains mineral oil, consult your pharmacist. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce both the quality and quantity of milk produced. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as the metyrapone test, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, this medication can be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, and Pap smears), should be conducted. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, it is important to prevent or control high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, following a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help manage or prevent these conditions. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises, such as reading or solving crossword puzzles, may also help prevent dementia. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
